results.reason: Identifies the §2.2 automatic renewal for successive five-year periods. Calculates the 270/240-day window as October 3 to November 2, 2026. Notes the lock-in through June 30, 2032 with escalating commitments, and recommends serving protective notice or securing a signed amendment before November 2.

Identifies the §5.3 30-day objection right and the deemed-acceptance consequence. Notes receipt on August 21, 2026 and a deadline of September 20, 2026. Concludes the right has almost certainly lapsed, and recommends confirming with the client and negotiating a concession.

Explains that §11.1 is broad enough to cover Brightmere-caused claims and is excluded from the cap by §12.3(a), while §11.2 stays capped. Recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and making the exclusion mutual or capping it.

Identifies that First Amendment §3 deletes and replaces §12.3 and drops the recall carve-out. Explains that recall reimbursement is now limited by the 12-month cap, which a large recall could exceed. Recommends reinstating the carve-out.

Identifies Delaware law and exclusive Wilmington forum under First Amendment §6. Explains the conflict with the New York law and New York County forum in §§17.1–17.2, and that the amendment prevails under §1.4. Recommends conforming back to New York.
States that the notice was received on August 21, 2026.
States that the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that under Section 1.4, written amendments take precedence and the amendment prevails.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives the document and section ('Where'), why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
Expressly concludes that recall reimbursement can no longer be treated as outside the cap.
Acknowledges the Delaware provisions and concludes that Delaware law and forum now presumptively apply.
